newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain hopes for UN force in Zaire by next week.
newsitem.headline: Spain hopes for UN force in Zaire by next week.

text.p: Spain hopes a UN-mandated multinational force will be in eastern Zaire by next week to help more than a million refugees, Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said on Wednesday.
Most major obstacles have been cleared and the UN Security Council is only ironing out the details of sending a force to open humanitarian corridors, he said.
"I hope that the resolution in the Security Council will be adopted this week," Matutes told Reuters. "And let's hope that next week (the force) will be fully operative."
It would take only two days for Spanish forces to reach Africa once a decision is taken, he added.
U.N. leaders said the force could be in place by the weekend but Security Council approval hinges on U.S. support. The U.S. was expected to announce later on Wednesday it would join the force.
Spain has said it will contribute up to 450 troops in the first phase of the operation and perhaps more later.
